name: Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʿtazz bi-llāh
summary: ʿAbbāsid prince and poet, pupil of al-Mubarrad and Thaʿlab, author of Kitāb al-Badīʿ, caliph for a day in 296/908 and killed after it.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls ʿAbd Allāh, son of the caliph al-Muʿtazz, a man of abundant merit, outstanding in letters, whose poetry was fine and plentiful; he quotes some of it and notes that he was proclaimed Commander of the Faithful.
He was raised caliph in Baghdad in 296/908, deposed within a day and killed. His Kitāb al-Badīʿ is the first book on the figures of style.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 299–301
